clue.text: Traditional postprandial custom should get us through immigration

parts.note: something traditional is thought of as typically British, so the word can stand for the national adjective
after a formal dinner the decanter of port is passed round the table, so the custom is to pass port

explanation.surface: Diners keeping up the old after-dinner ritual hope it will see them through border control.
explanation.walkthrough: Passing the port to the left after dinner is a long-standing British table custom; written as one word it becomes the travel document.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport issued by the UK is the document a Briton shows to clear border control on returning home.

clue.text: French poet that is missing in climbing party can't get home like this

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other, the poet's remains inside the party
in a down clue climbing means the word party is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: missing tells us that 'that is' drops out of the poet's name

parts.note: Paul Verlaine was a French Symbolist poet
i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is' (id est)

explanation.surface: A French poet goes missing on a mountaineering trip whose members cannot make it back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing party' looks like mountaineers, but 'climbing' turns the party (DO) upwards in this down clue to OD, which wraps the trimmed poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling by land rather than by air or sea is impossible when home is an island across the water.

clue.text: Song of 6 when temper's lost

indicators.note: lost signals that the quarrel is removed from the town's name

parts.note: the answer to 6 down, a Cumbrian town
a spat is a brief fit of bad temper, a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: A song from a small town, sung once someone's temper has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The 6 is the answer to 6 down; take SPAT out of ASPATRIA and ARIA remains.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera or oratorio.

clue.text: 16 song by drinker about to gain warmth — and curse about draw first

annotationWithheld.why: Clue '16 song by drinker about to gain warmth — and curse about draw first' for SWING LOW SWEET CHARIOT: no parse found that builds the pieces from drinker, warmth, curse and draw; needs a source for the wordplay.
annotationWithheld.clue: 16 song by drinker about to gain warmth — and curse about draw first

clue.text: Round part of English game raised the French

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the chosen part is written bottom to top
only part of the game's name is used, its final letters falling away

parts.note: cricket, the bat-and-ball game invented in England
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A rounded section of a cricket field is lifted by the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' works because this is a down clue, so the letters are written upwards; LE is the French for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A circle is a perfectly round shape, and round as a noun can mean a ring.

clue.text: Cumbrian town like the Fatherland?

parts.note: as means like, in the same way as
patria is Latin for fatherland, one's native country

explanation.surface: A northern English town is asked whether it resembles Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Fatherland' suggests Germany, but the setter wants the Latin word for it. Cumbria is a county in the far north-west of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspatria is a small market town in the county of Cumbria, north-west England.

clue.text: To stop taking sides is to be partial?

indicators.note: to be partial is to be only part of something, so the answer is a part of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone argues that refusing to take sides is itself a kind of bias.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partial' reads as biased, but it means taking only part of 'sides is to'.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to cease or refrain from doing something.

clue.text: Message sent to feast over 16 (if not 20)

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed over the second
sent in the sense of sent into confusion stirs up these letters

parts.note: 16 is the Rugby World Cup; rugby that is not league (20) is rugby union, hence the union

explanation.surface: A message is dispatched to a celebration of rugby, provided it's not the league code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent' stirs TO FEAST into STATE OF; 'over' places it above THE UNION. Rugby has two codes, union and league.
explanation.definitionFit: The State of the Union is the annual address the US President delivers to Congress.

clue.text: Most of Arkwright's work I've entered under Bridge

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other, the I've entering the reworked letters
work as a verb, to knead or shape, signals the letters are rearranged
most of the name is kept, with its last letters cut away

parts.note: Richard Arkwright, the inventor of the spinning frame, taken here as his surname's letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Most of an industrial inventor's output has found its way under a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: ARKWRI (Arkwright cut short by 'Most of') is shuffled by 'work' to RRKWAI, and IVE enters after the first R. The definition alludes to the film The Bridge on the River Kwai.
explanation.definitionFit: The film title The Bridge on the River Kwai places that river directly beneath the bridge.

clue.text: See 4
Landslip to entertain (with splits)

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Landslip to entertain (with splits)' for TERRAIN: no parse found that accounts for 'with splits' and builds the letters from the clue words.

clue.text: See 4
Bridge of a quarter of a yard

definitions.meaning: to bridge something is to stretch across it, and the noun names the stretch between supports
the ... of a hand, thumb to little finger, is nine inches, a quarter of a yard

explanation.definitionFit: Span is both the distance a bridge crosses and an old nine-inch hand measure.

clue.text: Almost assert aquatic beast's return? Not so fast!

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for assert is cut

parts.note: to allege is to assert

indicators.note: return signals the animal's name is read backwards

parts.note: an otter is an aquatic mammal

explanation.surface: Someone nearly claims a water creature is coming back, then urges caution.
explanation.walkthrough: ALLEG from ALLEGE (cut by 'Almost') is followed by RETTO, OTTER turned by 'return'.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegretto is a musical tempo marking meaning fairly brisk, a little slower than allegro.

clue.text: Lots of sheets pull somewhere in Cornwall

parts.note: a pad is a block of sheets of paper
to tow is to pull

explanation.surface: Bundles of bedding are dragged off to a Cornish destination.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at the south-western tip of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Padstow is a fishing town on the north coast of Cornwall.

clue.text: English 19 now beaten by Dutch bowler and public relations guy

indicators.note: beaten as in eggs beaten up, so these letters are mixed together

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: England's prize is defeated by a Dutchman's hat and a spin doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is SILVERWARE: England won the Rugby World Cup in 2003. A bowler here is a hat or a cricketer, not a trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: When the puzzle appeared England had just won the Rugby World Cup, making the trophy their silverware of the moment.

clue.text: It's unspecified intelligence about overheads

indicators.note: about tells us the cleverness wraps round the headgear

parts.note: wit is mental sharpness, intelligence
hats are worn over heads

explanation.surface: Something vague is said about cleverness and running costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overheads' looks like business costs, but here it means things worn over the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A whatsit is a word for a thing whose name one has forgotten or does not specify.

clue.text: See 16
Eat flesh to produce psychic disorder

indicators.note: the letters are worked into something new, producing a different word

explanation.surface: Eating meat is claimed to cause mental illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathing of oneself is a damaging psychological condition.

clue.text: Prizes for runners-up?

parts.note: second place in a race earns a silver medal, so prizes made of that metal suit those who come second

explanation.surface: A question about what second-placed finishers take home.
explanation.definitionFit: Silverware is slang for trophies, and silver medals go to those finishing second.

clue.text: Agreement at a distance

definitions.meaning: an alliance or compact between parties
an old measure of distance, about three miles

explanation.definitionFit: League is both an alliance of parties and an old unit of about three miles.

clue.text: Place for boats on Eastern river

parts.note: a wharf is a quay where boats moor
E is the abbreviation for East or Eastern

explanation.surface: A mooring stands on a river in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wharfe is a river in Yorkshire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wharfe flows through Wharfedale in Yorkshire.

clue.text: Turn with leg break achievable on this pot

indicators.note: a break breaks the letters up, rearranging them

parts.note: U is a U-turn
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricketer's spin delivery, a leg break, might help pot something.
explanation.walkthrough: A leg break is a spin delivery in cricket, but here 'break' rearranges U and LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: A glue-pot holds the adhesive, so what you get on such a pot is that sticky substance.

clue.text: Hydra to be left with article held by poor Paul

indicators.note: held by places the other pieces inside the reworked name
poor suggests the name is in bad shape, rearranged

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Poor Paul is left holding a water monster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges PAUL to PULA, which holds L and AN. A Hydra is also a tiny freshwater animal, not just the myth.
explanation.definitionFit: A planula is the free-swimming larva of hydras and other cnidarians, so it is a hydra yet to develop.

clue.text: Aquatic beast ran off from Churchill home

indicators.note: off from means the running word is taken away from the name

parts.note: Randolph Churchill, Winston's father and also his son
in means at home

explanation.surface: A creature runs away from Winston Churchill's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Churchill home' suggests Chartwell, his house; instead take RAN from RANDOLPH and add IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolphin is a marine mammal of the whale family.

clue.text: Student receiving award by ear?

parts.note: L is a learner, a student driver
OBE is the Order of the British Empire, an honour

explanation.surface: A student is honoured for playing music by ear.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour given by the monarch. The definition is cryptic: the lobe is what hangs by the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: The earlobe is the soft lower part of the outer ear.

clue.text: Line makes a funny noise

indicators.note: together with noise, this says the word is spoken, not spelt
a noise is a sound heard, so the spelling follows how the word is said

parts.note: rum is old slang for funny, odd

explanation.surface: A row of people makes an amusing sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' meaning odd is dated British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhumb line is a course crossing every meridian at the same angle, used in navigation.

clue.text: 8 soldier may pull through

definitions.meaning: eight is four multiplied by two
soldiers clean a rifle barrel by pulling through a strip of flannel of that size, four inches by two

explanation.definitionFit: Four times two is eight, and four-by-two is the army's name for rifle-cleaning flannel.
